# EU Funding News · Ullswater Investments — full text of recent articles

## EIT HEI Call 2026: up to €1.25M for university-led deep-tech consortia
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/eit-hei-call-2026-universities-deep-tech/
Date: 2026-11-09 · Category: Horizon Europe · Source: EIT Higher Education Initiative (https://eit-hei.eu/funding-support/funding-opportunities/open-calls/call-for-proposals-2026/)

The EIT Higher Education Initiative is funding HEI-led consortia that build deep-tech and manufacturing innovation capacity. Deadline: 13 January 2027.

- Programme: EIT Higher Education Initiative (EIT HEI), Call for Proposals 2026
- Funding: Up to €1.25 million per project
- Project duration: 18 months, 1 May 2027 – 31 October 2028
- Deadline: 13 January 2027, 17:00 CET
- Minimum consortium: 5 partners, incl. 3 HEIs from 3 countries and 2 business partners
- Results: March 2027

The EIT Higher Education Initiative opened its Call for Proposals 2026 on 20 October 2026. It funds projects that help universities and other higher education institutions turn STEM talent, knowledge and research into deep-tech and manufacturing innovation and entrepreneurship. Each project can receive up to €1.25 million over 18 months, from 1 May 2027 to 31 October 2028.
Projects are expected to work on three connected fronts: developing talent, strengthening the institution's capacity to valorise knowledge and innovate, and linking the institution to regional and European innovation ecosystems. Eligible activities include innovation action plans, entrepreneurship programmes, training and mentoring, new or stronger innovation structures inside the institution, technology transfer and start-up creation.
Applications come from consortia led by a higher education institution. The minimum is five organisations, all in Horizon Europe eligible countries, with at least three higher education institutions from three different countries (one of them in an EU Member State) and at least two business or industry partners, which may be networks or associations. Research organisations, transfer offices, public bodies, intermediaries, social enterprises and NGOs can also join.
Applicants complete the HEInnovate self-assessment and an Innovation Vision Action Plan, register in the EU Participant Portal and submit through the EIT HEI application portal. The deadline is 13 January 2027 at 17:00 CET, and results are due in March 2027. Online info sessions run until 3 December, covering KPI expectations, application and budget planning, an EIT KIC Discovery Day and an open Q&A.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Ullswater Investments analysis: the business-partner requirement is the detail to watch. Every consortium needs at least two companies or industry associations, so universities will be looking for industrial partners in deep tech and manufacturing over the next weeks, and companies have a direct route into university-led innovation projects. With a January deadline and two months left, the consortium should be closed in November so that December can go into the action plan and budget. Spanish universities that want to coordinate should start with the HEInnovate self-assessment, which shapes the rest of the proposal.

---

## EU and India conclude talks on India joining Horizon Europe
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/india-horizon-europe-association-concluded/
Date: 2026-11-06 · Category: Research Policy · Source: European Commission – EURAXESS India (https://euraxess.ec.europa.eu/worldwide/india/news/eu-india-eu-and-india-conclude-negotiations-association-horizon-europe)

Association is envisaged for January 2027. Indian organisations would then be able to receive funding directly and lead Pillar II collaborative projects.

- Programme: Horizon Europe (2021–2027), budget €93.5 billion
- Association envisaged: January 2027
- Negotiations: Exploratory talks from 6 February 2026; formal talks from 17 July 2026
- Next step: Formal signature, once both sides complete their procedures

The European Commission and India have finished negotiating India's association to Horizon Europe, the EU's research and innovation programme for 2021–2027. Association is the closest form of cooperation open to countries outside the EU, and it is envisaged to apply from January 2027.
Once the agreement is in force, organisations based in India would be able to receive Horizon Europe funding directly and to lead collaborative projects under Pillar II, which covers global challenges and European industrial competitiveness. Areas highlighted for joint work include health, digital technologies, industry, space, climate, energy and the bioeconomy.
The arrangements do not yet apply. Closing the negotiations clears the way for the agreement to be signed, which depends on both sides completing their internal procedures. The talks began with exploratory discussions on 6 February 2026, and formal negotiations opened on 17 July 2026.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): For European consortia, this widens the pool of partners that can take part on equal terms with EU organisations. Indian universities, research bodies and companies are likely to start appearing more often in Pillar II proposals, including as coordinators. Teams planning for 2027 calls should talk to Indian partners early, but should not count on the new terms until the agreement has entered into force. Until then, the current participation rules for India continue to apply.

## EIC 2027 work programme opens over €1.8 billion for deep tech
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/eic-2027-work-programme-1-8-billion/
Date: 2026-11-05 · Category: EIC, Defence & Equity · Source: European Innovation Council (https://eic.ec.europa.eu/eic-funding-opportunities/eic-funding-opportunities-2027_en)

The Commission has adopted the EIC's 2027 plan: €578 million for the Accelerator, €248 million for Pathfinder and €100 million for a defence equity call.

- Total: Over €1.8 billion
- EIC Accelerator: €578 million (grants below €2.5 million, investments €0.5–10 million)
- EIC Pathfinder: €248 million (grants up to €4 million)
- STEP Scale Up: €290 million (investments €10–30 million)
- STEP Scale Up Defence: €100 million (up to €30 million direct equity)
- Scaleup Europe Fund: €400 million

The European Commission has adopted the European Innovation Council's work programme for 2027, which puts more than €1.8 billion on the table for strategic technologies and for companies that want to scale up. The money is spread across six main schemes, from early-stage research to large equity rounds.
The EIC Accelerator remains the largest line at €578 million for start-ups and SMEs, combining grants below €2.5 million with investments of €0.5 million to €10 million. Pathfinder receives €248 million for multi-disciplinary research teams, with grants of up to €4 million, while Transition has €92 million and grants of up to €2.5 million to turn research results into innovation. A further €25 million goes to the Advanced Innovation Challenges, which pay a €300,000 lump sum.
At the scale-up end, STEP Scale Up has €290 million for investments of €10 million to €30 million, and a dedicated STEP Scale Up Defence call has €100 million with up to €30 million in direct equity. The Scaleup Europe Fund receives €400 million for equity investments above €30 million, reaching up to several hundred million euro.
According to the EIC, the 2027 programme completes the funding for three instruments introduced during 2026: the Scaleup Europe Fund (€1 billion), defence investments (€200 million) and the Advanced Innovation Challenges pilot (€25 million). A redesigned Women TechEU programme doubles its grants to €150,000 per start-up. The EIC will present its 2027 funding opportunities at an online information day on 19 November, followed by a session on the EIC Accelerator Challenges on 20 November.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): With the 2027 budget now fixed, applicants can plan their calendar against a known envelope rather than estimates. The Accelerator stays the main entry point for start-ups and SMEs, but the growing weight of equity instruments shows the EIC increasingly expects companies to arrive with an investment case, not only a technology case. Dual-use and defence companies now have a recurring, dedicated route. Teams should read the full work programme and call texts before choosing a scheme, as rules and evaluation steps can change from one year to the next.

## EIC sets 19 November info day on its 2027 funding opportunities
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/eic-2027-funding-info-day/
Date: 2026-11-05 · Category: EIC, Defence & Equity · Source: European Innovation Council (https://eic.ec.europa.eu/events/online-information-day-eic-funding-opportunities-2027-2026-11-19_en)

The online session will present Work Programme 2027 scheme by scheme, from Pathfinder to STEP Defence. Registration closes on 18 November.

- Event: EIC Work Programme 2027 online information day
- Date: 19 November 2026, 09:30–15:40 CET
- Registration closes: 18 November 2026, 09:30 CET
- Format: Online, in English
- Follow-up sessions: Accelerator Challenges, 20 November 2026; Advanced Innovation Challenges, 3 February 2027

The European Innovation Council will present its 2027 funding opportunities at an online information day on 19 November 2026. The session, organised with its executive agency EISMEA and the Commission's research directorate-general, is held in English and will open with the main changes in Work Programme 2027.
The agenda then goes through the schemes one at a time: Pathfinder, Transition, Accelerator, STEP and STEP Defence, followed by Business Acceleration Services, Access2EIC and EEN2EIC. Pathfinder and Transition get the longest slots, at 90 minutes each.
Registration closes on 18 November at 09:30 CET. Two further sessions follow: one on the EIC Accelerator Challenges on 20 November 2026 and another on the EIC Advanced Innovation Challenges on 3 February 2027.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Companies planning an EIC application next year should treat this as the first checkpoint. Rule changes between work programmes can affect eligibility, the shape of a proposal and the choice of scheme, so it is worth attending before drafting starts. Dual-use and defence companies should note that STEP Defence has its own place on the agenda. Applicants should base their plans on the published work programme rather than on the previous year's rules, and use the advance question channel to raise any points specific to their project.

## CDTI Innovación commits €12.75 million to 19 R&D+I projects
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/cdti-council-19-projects-october/
Date: 2026-11-04 · Category: Spain · Source: CDTI Innovación (https://www.cdti.es/noticias/consejo-cdti-innovacion-destina-mas-12-millones-euros-19-nuevos-proyectos-idi-empresarial)

All 19 October approvals are loans. Ten companies get CDTI funding for the first time, 15 are SMEs and 13 operations are co-financed by POPE.

- Approved: October 2026, CDTI Innovación governing council
- Projects: 19, all in the loan modality
- Total budget: €17.21 million
- CDTI contribution: €12.75 million, including a €2.47 million non-reimbursable tranche
- Companies: 19, of which 10 first-time recipients and 15 SMEs
- EU co-financing: 13 operations under POPE 2021-2027

The governing council of CDTI Innovación, the public business entity attached to Spain's Ministry of Science, Innovation and Universities, signed off 19 new business R&D+I projects in October. Their combined budget is €17.21 million, of which CDTI will contribute €12.75 million. Every project takes the form of a loan, and together they carry a non-reimbursable tranche of €2.47 million.
Most of the money sits in the Línea Directa de Expansión, with 13 projects and a CDTI contribution of €8,926,650.13. The Línea Directa de Innovación accounts for four projects and €3,266,716.13, while the two Proyectos de I+D receive €561,233.83 and show the highest financing rate of the three, at 85%.
Thirteen of the 19 operations are co-financed by the Programa Operativo Plurirregional de España (POPE) 2021-2027. That programme lets CDTI offer a non-reimbursable tranche of up to 30% on co-financed projects, whatever the size of the beneficiary. Murcia is the largest region in this round, with five operations and a CDTI contribution of €5,851,458.95.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): The profile of this round is encouraging for newcomers: most of the companies are SMEs, and just over half had never received CDTI money before. CDTI's direct lines are therefore a realistic entry point for firms without a funding track record. The POPE rule deserves attention at planning stage, because whether a project qualifies for co-financing can change how much of a loan does not need repaying, and that holds for larger companies as well as SMEs. Applicants should check eligibility for their region and instrument before settling on a financing structure.

## Open Research Europe becomes fee-free in 11 countries
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/open-research-europe-fee-free-11-countries/
Date: 2026-11-03 · Category: Research Policy · Source: European Commission – Research and Innovation (https://research-and-innovation.ec.europa.eu/news/all-research-and-innovation-news/eligibility-publish-open-research-europe-without-fees-expands-researchers-11-countries-2026-11-03_en)

Researchers in 11 countries can now publish on the Commission's open-access platform without publication fees, under a collective funding model.

- Platform: Open Research Europe (European Commission open-access publishing)
- Change: No publication fees for researchers in 11 countries
- Model: Collective funding
- Details: Eligible countries and conditions in the official announcement

Researchers in 11 countries can now publish in Open Research Europe, the European Commission's open-access publishing platform, without paying publication fees, under a collective funding model.
The official announcement lists the eligible countries and the conditions.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Open-access publication is mandatory for Horizon Europe results. A fee-free route reduces the dissemination costs that consortia must budget for, so it is worth checking eligibility before fixing the dissemination budget in a proposal.

## EU and Bpifrance plan €150 million guarantee for Ukraine partnerships
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/11/bpifrance-eu-guarantees-ukraine-dual-use-partnerships/
Date: 2026-11-03 · Category: EIC, Defence & Equity · Source: European Commission – Enlargement and Eastern Neighbourhood (https://enlargement.ec.europa.eu/news/bpifrance-et-la-commission-europeenne-signent-un-accord-pour-accelerer-les-partenariats-industriels-2026-11-03_en)

The arrangement under the Ukraine Investment Framework targets French–Ukrainian industrial ties in defence and dual-use technology.

- Instrument: Ukraine Investment Framework
- EU support: €150 million in guarantees and €13 million in grants
- Bpifrance target: More than €480 million in financial interventions over three years
- Partnerships: 30 over three years, French companies and Ukrainian startups
- Status: Envisaged; final legal agreements still pending

Bpifrance and the European Commission's Directorate-General for Enlargement and Eastern Neighbourhood announced the arrangement during European Defence Week in Paris, which runs from 2 to 6 November 2026. Under the Ukraine Investment Framework, the EU would provide €150 million in guarantees and €13 million in grants, with Bpifrance aiming for more than €480 million in financial interventions over three years.
The instruments would be aimed at French companies developing in Ukraine, Ukrainian companies buying French goods and equipment, and French firms partnering with local companies. Priority sectors include aerial, land and maritime drones, electronic protection, space, communications, navigation and critical components, with a focus on dual-use technologies. Energy, digital and industrial equipment are also covered.
A non-financial strand foresees 30 partnerships over three years between French companies and Ukrainian startups in defence and dual-use technologies, supported by EuroQuity, Bpifrance's international matchmaking platform.
The deal is not final. Legal agreements depend on the Commission's inter-service consultation being completed and on the contractual documentation being finalised.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): The scheme is reserved for French-linked operations, so most European applicants cannot use it directly. Its interest lies in the model: an EU guarantee channelled through a national promotional bank to support dual-use industrial partnerships with Ukraine. Companies elsewhere in Europe may want to ask their own national institutions whether similar routes exist. The announcement gives no detailed eligibility criteria, so French firms should wait for the final terms.

## Commission proposes €31.7 billion for Ukraine's defence industry
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/10/ukraine-support-loan-2027-defence-industry/
Date: 2026-10-30 · Category: EIC, Defence & Equity · Source: European Commission – Enlargement and Eastern Neighbourhood (https://enlargement.ec.europa.eu/news/commission-takes-key-step-forward-2027-financial-support-ukraine-2026-10-30_en)

The proposal covers 2027 under the €90 billion Ukraine Support Loan. The Council still has to adopt it before disbursements start.

- Proposal date: 30 October 2026
- 2027 tranche: €45 billion remaining under the €90 billion loan
- Defence industrial capacity 2027: €31.7 billion
- Budget support 2027: Up to €13.3 billion
- 2026 defence allocation: €28.3 billion, of which €15.8 billion disbursed for defence procurement
- Next step: Council implementing decision; disbursements planned for early 2027

The European Commission adopted a package on 30 October 2026 that asks the Council to approve the remaining €45 billion for 2027 under the €90 billion Ukraine Support Loan. Of that sum, €31.7 billion would go to Ukraine's defence industrial capacity and up to €13.3 billion to budget support, split equally between the Ukraine Facility and Macro-Financial Assistance.
Across 2026 and 2027 the loan reserves €60 billion for defence capabilities and defence industrial capacity and €30 billion for budget support. The Council allocated €28.3 billion to defence industrial capacity for 2026 in a decision of 23 April 2026, and €15.8 billion of that has been disbursed for defence procurement.
The package follows Ukraine's Financing Strategy, submitted on 26 October 2026 and assessed positively by the Commission. The Council must now adopt the implementing decision, after which Member States will decide the allocations. Disbursements are planned for early 2027 once the assistance is adopted. Budget support remains tied to conditions on the rule of law, anti-corruption, economic resilience and sustainability.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): This is a sizeable defence-industrial envelope, but it is not a grant call: nothing here opens for applications. Companies in defence and dual-use supply chains should treat it as a demand signal and watch the Council decision and the allocation stage. The practical question for suppliers is how procurement under the loan will be organised, so they should follow the official rules rather than assume access.

## Canada joins EuroHPC as a Participating State
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/10/canada-joins-eurohpc-supercomputing-network/
Date: 2026-10-30 · Category: Digital & AI · Source: European Commission – Shaping Europe's digital future (https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/eu-and-canada-team-supercomputing-and-quantum)

Agreed at the EU–Canada Summit in Montreal, the move opens Europe's public supercomputing, AI and quantum resources to Canada.

- Announced: 30 October 2026, EU–Canada Summit, Montreal
- New status: Canada is a Participating State in the EuroHPC JU
- EuroHPC JU network: 12 supercomputers procured, 19 AI Factories, 13 AI Factory Antennas
- Governing board: European Commission and 39 Participating States
- Horizon Europe link: Canada associated since 2024
- Legal basis of wider mandate: Council Regulation (EU) 2026/150

Canada became a Participating State in the European High-Performance Computing Joint Undertaking (EuroHPC JU) on 30 October 2026, during the EU–Canada Summit in Montreal. The step gives Canada use of the joint undertaking's high-performance computing, AI and quantum resources, and lets Canadian scientists work alongside European counterparts.
The two sides say they want closer cooperation across supercomputing, AI infrastructure and quantum technology, with a view to developing scientific applications and raising the innovation potential of companies. It builds on research cooperation going back to 1996; Canada has also been associated with Horizon Europe since 2024.
EuroHPC JU has so far procured 12 supercomputers, oversees 19 AI Factories and 13 AI Factory Antennas, and is deploying a European quantum computing infrastructure. The European Commission and 39 Participating States sit on its governing board, and Council Regulation (EU) 2026/150 extended its mandate to AI Gigafactories and quantum technologies.
The summit produced related digital outcomes: Destination Earth will take on Canadian cooperation in AI-powered climate modelling, and the parties discussed Arctic connectivity and the interoperability of EU and Canadian digital identities.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): For consortia in AI, HPC and quantum, Canadian partners now sit closer to the same compute ecosystem as their European counterparts, on top of the existing Horizon Europe association. That can make EU–Canada collaboration more practical to design into a proposal. Applicants should still check the access rules and eligibility conditions of each specific call before building a work plan around EuroHPC resources.

## Horizon Europe opens 14 'Health' topics for 2027, due 17 February
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/10/horizon-europe-health-2027-calls-open/
Date: 2026-10-29 · Category: Health & Health Data · Source: European Health and Digital Executive Agency (HaDEA) (https://hadea.ec.europa.eu/news/2027-horizon-europe-health-calls-are-open-proposals-2026-10-29_en)

HaDEA has published the 2027 'Health' calls, from antivirals and antimicrobials to AI biomarkers and point-of-care diagnostics. Info day on 26 November.

- Programme: Horizon Europe, Cluster 1 'Health'
- Topics: 14 topics in the 2027 calls
- Deadline: 17 February 2027, 17:00 Brussels time
- Info day: 26 November 2026
- Next openings: Pandemic Preparedness Partnership (Phase 2) expected 10 February 2027; Cancer Mission calls February 2027

The European Health and Digital Executive Agency (HaDEA) has announced that the 2027 Horizon Europe 'Health' calls are open on the EU Funding and Tenders Portal. Proposals must be submitted by 17 February 2027 at 17:00 Brussels time.
The 14 topics cover a wide range. On infectious disease, they include new small-molecule antivirals for pathogens with epidemic potential, monoclonal antibodies against several virus families including Flaviviruses, and innovative antimicrobials against resistant pathogens. Other topics address non-communicable diseases, clinical trials for neurodegenerative diseases, chronic disease prevention in children and young people, disabilities and independent living, and the health effects of climate change.
Several topics are aimed at technology developers: AI-based predictive biomarkers of disease progression and treatment response, cell-free protein synthesis platforms for biologicals, portable point-of-care diagnostics, and personalised approaches to reduce adverse drug reactions caused by multiple medications. Some of the topics run as two-stage calls.
A Cluster 1 'Health' info day on 26 November 2026 will present the 2027 topics. HaDEA also signals further calls: the European Partnership for Pandemic Preparedness (Phase 2) is expected to open on 10 February 2027, EU Cancer Mission calls will open in February 2027, and additional calls will follow in June 2027.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): With a single February deadline, consortia have roughly three months to build partnerships and write proposals, which is tight for clinical and multi-country work. The two-stage topics lower the effort of a first submission but leave little room for a weak concept. The AI biomarker, diagnostics and protein-synthesis topics are a natural fit for health-tech and biotech SMEs that can bring an industrial angle to academic consortia. Applicants should check each topic's conditions on the Funding and Tenders Portal and use the info day to test their fit before committing.

## First EIC defence equity call closes with nine applications
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/10/eic-step-scale-up-defence-call-closes/
Date: 2026-10-29 · Category: EIC, Defence & Equity · Source: European Innovation Council (https://eic.ec.europa.eu/news/overview-eic-step-scale-defence-call-submissions-2026-10-29_en)

The EIC STEP Scale Up Defence call offered direct equity of up to €30 million per company; results are expected in early 2027.

- Call: EIC STEP Scale Up Defence
- Closed: 28 October 2026
- Applications: 9 from 7 countries
- Instrument: Direct equity, up to €30 million per company
- Budget: €100 million
- Results: Expected early 2027

The first EIC STEP Scale Up Defence call closed on 28 October with nine applications from seven countries.
It is the first EU funding instrument to offer direct equity, up to €30 million per company, to firms whose technologies serve primarily defence purposes, from air and missile defence to drones and counter-drone systems.
The call has a €100 million budget and results are expected in early 2027. Dual-use innovators can apply through the EIC Accelerator and the general STEP Scale Up call.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Defence is now an equity market for the EIC, not just a grant topic. Companies with dual-use technologies do not need a dedicated defence call: the EIC Accelerator and the general STEP Scale Up call remain open routes, and a well-prepared investment case matters as much as the technology.

## Guidelines on generative AI in research get their largest update
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/10/generative-ai-research-guidelines-update/
Date: 2026-10-16 · Category: Research Policy · Source: European Commission – Research and Innovation (https://research-and-innovation.ec.europa.eu/news/all-research-and-innovation-news/era-living-guidelines-responsible-use-generative-ai-research-updated-2026-10-16_en)

The ERA Living Guidelines for researchers, research organisations and funders were updated on the same day the first 13 EOSC nodes went live.

- Document: ERA Living Guidelines on the responsible use of generative AI in research
- Audience: Researchers, research organisations and funders
- Change: Largest update so far
- Same day: First 13 nodes of the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) went live

The European Commission published the largest update so far of the ERA Living Guidelines on the responsible use of generative AI in research, the shared recommendations for researchers, research organisations and funders.
On the same day, the first 13 nodes of the European Open Science Cloud (EOSC) went live, expanding access to research data and digital services across Europe.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Evaluators and funders increasingly expect applicants to explain how they use generative AI responsibly. Aligning a proposal's methodology and data management plan with these guidelines is a simple way to avoid weaknesses in the implementation criterion.

## RAISE pledging initiative launched for AI in science
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/10/raise-pledging-initiative-ai-in-science/
Date: 2026-10-15 · Category: Digital & AI · Source: European Commission – Press Corner (https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/ip_26_2175)

Companies and philanthropic organisations are invited to support researchers who use AI, mainly with models, computing capacity, software, data and training.

- Initiative: RAISE pledging initiative (Resource for AI Science in Europe)
- Launched: European AI in Science Summit, Dublin
- Who can pledge: Companies and philanthropic organisations
- Type of support: Voluntary, mainly in kind: AI models, computing capacity, research software, data and training
- Also announced: Mistral AI–CERN partnership on a physics foundation model; RAISE Hub, Forum and Observatory live
- Review: Pledges reviewed every year

At the European AI in Science Summit in Dublin, the European Commission launched the RAISE pledging initiative, inviting companies and philanthropic organisations to support researchers who use AI in science.
Pledges are voluntary and mainly in kind: access to AI models, computing capacity, research software, data and training.
Mistral AI and CERN announced a partnership to develop the largest foundation model in physics, and the RAISE Hub, Forum and Observatory went live. Pledges will be reviewed every year.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): RAISE is becoming the EU's umbrella for AI in science, and it already has its own Horizon Europe call in Cluster 4. For technology providers, a pledge is a low-cost way to gain visibility with research organisations and with the Commission ahead of future RAISE funding rounds.

## Horizon Europe Cluster 4 opens its 2027 calls
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/10/cluster-4-opens-2027-calls/
Date: 2026-10-13 · Category: Digital & AI · Source: HaDEA – European Health and Digital Executive Agency (https://hadea.ec.europa.eu/programmes/horizon-europe_en)

Industry, two-stage and RAISE calls opened on 13 October; the digital call on federated and sustainable AI data processing opens on 17 November.

- Programme: Horizon Europe, Cluster 4 “Digital, Industry and Space”
- Industry call: HORIZON-CL4-2027-01 · €224.7 million · 11 topics
- Opened: 13 October 2026 (CL4-2027-01, two-stage CL4-2027-02 and RAISE)
- First deadline: 2 February 2027
- Digital call: HORIZON-CL4-2027-04 · opens 17 November 2026 · deadline 18 March 2027
- Next: €125 million Clean Industrial Deal call from 12 January 2027

The 2027 calls of Horizon Europe Cluster 4 “Digital, Industry and Space” are rolling out.
The industry call HORIZON-CL4-2027-01 (€224.7 million, 11 topics), the two-stage CL4-2027-02 and the RAISE call opened on 13 October with a first deadline of 2 February 2027.
The digital call HORIZON-CL4-2027-04, including topics on federated and sustainable AI data processing, opens on 17 November with a deadline of 18 March 2027. A €125 million Clean Industrial Deal call follows on 12 January 2027.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Cluster 4 is the main Horizon Europe entry point for industrial and digital companies. The topics on federated and sustainable AI data processing are directly relevant for organisations working on data spaces and sovereign AI. Two-stage calls lower the entry cost: a short first-stage proposal is enough to test the idea.

## New €230 million Horizon Europe call on nature
URL: https://news.ullswaterinvestments.com/2026/10/horizon-europe-230-million-call-nature/
Date: 2026-10-02 · Category: Horizon Europe · Source: European Commission – Research and Innovation (https://research-and-innovation.ec.europa.eu/news/all-research-and-innovation-news/horizon-europe-launches-new-research-and-innovation-call-nature-2026-10-02_en)

Ten topics to raise biodiversity spending across Pillar II of the 2026–2027 work programme, with most deadlines on 14 January 2027.

- Programme: Horizon Europe, Pillar II (Work Programme 2026–2027)
- Call: Transformative change towards a nature-positive economy and society
- Budget: €230 million
- Topics: 10, including PFAS effects on biodiversity, invasive species and biodiversity monitoring
- Main deadline: 14 January 2027
- Ocean observing action: €50 million innovation action, deadline 16 February 2027

The European Commission published a new €230 million Horizon Europe call, “Transformative change towards a nature-positive economy and society”, to raise biodiversity spending across Pillar II of the 2026–2027 work programme.
Its ten topics include the effects of PFAS on biodiversity and ecosystem services, invasive species and cost-effective biodiversity monitoring. Most topics close on 14 January 2027.
A separate €50 million innovation action for a stronger Global Ocean Observing System closes on 16 February 2027.

Why it matters (Ullswater Investments analysis): Biodiversity is no longer a niche for environmental research groups: topics on PFAS, monitoring and invasive species open the door to companies working on sensors, environmental data and analytical services. With most deadlines in mid-January, consortia that are not already formed need to start partner search now.
